headline.title: Pre-season: still too mild.
headline.text: None of the resorts close to opening get cold enough to make snow this week. Killington typically opens first, around Nov 8.

BTV.excerpt:
Temperatures increase this week, and there is the potential for some rain showers Tuesday and Tuesday night.
A late week cold front will bring several days of rain

ALY.excerpt: ) Mostly dry weather is expected through Wednesday, with increasing chances for rain later in the week into next weekend. Above normal temperatures will continue through the upcoming week.

GYX.excerpt: Temperatures will average above normal through the middle of the week with mostly dry weather. There is increasing confidence for appreciable precipitation late this week.

BUF.excerpt:
) Warm weather will continue through the week, with the warmest days expected on Tuesday and Wednesday.
) Unsettled weather returns to the region late in the week.

PHI.excerpt:
Some areas of frost again tonight. Otherwise, generally tranquil weather is expected to prevail through the middle portion of next week.
Rain chances are expected to return late this week into this weekend.

CTP.excerpt: ) Dry and mild weather will continue until late Wednesday or Wednesday night when we'll likely see some rain showers followed by slightly cooler weather.

RLX.excerpt: ) Some showers today, but more widespread and significant precipitation Wednesday into Thursday.

writeups.name: Vermont
writeups.title: Quiet and mild.
paras: Next two days: summit temperatures from {{t:32}} to {{t:57}}, with rain at times.
Killington usually opens first here, around Nov 8. Nights stay too mild to make much snow this week.
NWS Burlington forecasters, Sunday 6:55 PM: "Temperatures increase this week, and there is the potential for some rain showers Tuesday and Tuesday night."
writeups.outlook: Days 8 to 14: NOAA's outlook leans slightly warmer than normal and near-normal precipitation.
